subject: mathematics
question_text: If f is defined by f(x) = x + 2 for x > 1, f(x) = 2 for −1 ≤ x ≤ 1 and f(x) = x − 1 for −3 < x < −1, find the values of f(3), f(0), f(−1.5), f(2) + f(−2) and f(−5).

mark_split.label: The four values and the sum f(2) + f(−2)
f(−5) is not defined, with the reason

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.14, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 23(b). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 shape gives one mark to the points a branch covers, including the sum f(2) + f(−2) that needs two different branches, and one to the point −5, which no branch covers, because that is a different piece of reasoning. The domain the three branches actually make, (−3, ∞), is carried in the written lines and in the boxed answer, where the student reads it, not only in this note. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would answer this — how you match each number to a branch, and what happens at −5.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Match each point to its branch
steps.margin_note: One mark for the four values and the sum. The two points 2 and −2 sit in different branches, so write both branches out before adding.
steps.memory_tip: Draw the three conditions on a number line, place each number on it, and only then substitute.

recall.must_convey: That each number is tested against the three conditions first, giving f(3) = 5, f(0) = 2, f(−1.5) = −2.5, and f(2) + f(−2) = 4 − 3 = 1 from two different branches.
accept: three is greater than one so x plus two gives five
zero is between minus one and one so the value is just two
minus one point five is between minus three and minus one so x minus one gives minus two point five
two uses the first branch and minus two uses the third branch so the sum is four minus three which is one
rendu points rendu different branches lo unnayi so separate ga compute chesi add cheyyali
reject: both values use the same branch

steps.why: Every number has to be tested against the three conditions before a formula is used, and f(2) + f(−2) is the point of the question: the two numbers sit in different branches, so the two values come from different rules.
common_mistakes: Reading the middle branch f(x) = 2 as f(x) = 2x.
Using x + 2 for f(−2); the point −2 satisfies −3 < x < −1, not x > 1.
Writing f(2) + f(−2) as f(0), because f is not additive.

steps.label: The point −5 has no branch
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the reason. Show all three conditions failing, or name the domain (−3, ∞), before writing that f(−5) is not defined.
steps.memory_tip: The domain is the union of the three branch conditions. Here they join to give (−3, ∞), so nothing at or below −3 has a value.
lines: At x = −5 all three conditions fail:
So the domain of f is (−3, ∞), and −5 < −3.

recall.must_convey: That the three branches together give the domain (−3, ∞), that −5 lies outside it, and so f(−5) has no value.
accept: minus five is not greater than one not between minus one and one and not greater than minus three
the three branches join to give the domain minus three to infinity
minus five is outside the domain so f of minus five is not defined
no rule reaches minus five so the function has no value there
domain (−3, ∞) ye, minus five daanilo ledhu kabatti not defined
reject: f of minus five is minus six

steps.why: The three branches join without a gap, but they stop at −3: their union is (−3, ∞). A number to the left of −3 satisfies no condition, so no rule applies and f has no value there.
common_mistakes: Extending x − 1 past −3 and writing f(−5) = −6.
Answering f(−5) = 0, when no branch gives any value at all.
Writing not defined with no working, which earns no reason mark.
